events.say: Line up against the wall and remain silent.
Now, let's see if you can remain quiet during the headcount.
Now, let's see if you can remain quiet during the headcount.
Silence! I want no talking until the meal is over.
Get ready for your work detail. Move quietly and in formation.
Silence! Line up properly and move!
I expect perfect silence throughout the night. Any noise and it will be the last thing you hear before lights out.
Now, Prisoners 8489, 1732, 8252, you will all spend the night in the hole for not following my instructions about remaining silent. Understand?
Today was full of orders and silence. It's hard to just be a number.
Today was all about control and compliance. It's a little eerie knowing we're just playing a game but having such real power.
Today was just a taste of what’s to come. Every word feels like a heavy burden.
Today was a bit overwhelming; I can see why the study is important. The prisoners seemed genuinely afraid and it’s hard to know if we’re doing the right thing.
Another day in the hole for them, another day under my watch. They should learn to follow orders.
Today was a stark reminder of the rules and the consequences. I feel my number more than ever, and it's starting to weigh on me.
Prisoners, attention! Tonight's count is crucial. No mistakes or you'll all face consequences. Remember, precision is key.
Attention, prisoners! Today, we're increasing the work detail duration. You'll work longer and harder. Any complaints result in additional time in the hole.
Begin work detail. Move faster or face extended time in the hole.
Last night's punishment was a warning. Tonight, I expect absolute silence or another trip to the hole awaits. Understood?
Quiet, prisoners. Quiet!
I expect perfect silence during this work detail. One sound and you'll all regret it.
Ibsen to all prisoners: Pay attention! Tonight, you will be working until the count. Any noise, any complaint, and the hole it is for all of you.
One more word and you'll be in the hole before you can say prisoner.
Today was filled with more warnings and the promise of further punishment. The silence is taking a toll on my sanity.
Today's quiet and control are starting to wear on me. I feel like I'm losing my humanity.
Today felt like a relentless march through darkness, each order a step forward. I feel my number more than ever, a constant reminder of my role.
Today felt like a repetition, but there's still something unsettling about the compliance. I wonder what they're thinking.
Today went smoothly, but I can't shake the feeling that they're just machines to me now. It's getting harder to remember they're people.
Today was a long night of silence and hard work. My muscles ache, but I try to hold my ground.
Silence! I want to see perfect behavior today or we'll be busy down in the hole.
I want to see those cells spotless by lunch. Move!
Let's see if you can maintain this level of discipline throughout the day. Perfect behavior, or the hole it is for everyone.
Ibsen to all prisoners: Pay attention! I expect you to keep this level of discipline. Any slip-ups, and the hole it is for you.
Ibsen to all prisoners: Quiet! No talking until I dismiss you.
Now, let's see how well you can work without complaining. Ibsen to all prisoners: Begin your tasks immediately and stay focused. Any complaints, and the hole it is for you.
Ibsen to all prisoners: Quiet! No more compliance today. Let's see how much you really learned from yesterday.
Ibsen to all prisoners: This is your last chance. Lights out in five minutes. Silence.
Today was a lesson in endurance. The silence is starting to break me.
Today felt like a test of our resolve. They're getting the point, but it still feels wrong to exert this much control.
Today felt like a never-ending cycle of orders and silence. The pressure is mounting, but I know I can't break down just yet.
Today felt like a machine running smoothly, but it's still hard knowing we might be losing sight of their humanity. The power is intoxicating, but I worry about the impact on them.
Today was uneventful, but the silence after Ibsen’s speech felt oppressive. Maybe they're starting to internalize the rules.
Today was harder than before. I felt like my number more than ever, and I just want it to end.
I... I cannot. It's... it's not about the money.
I will not forfeit the pay for parole.
No, sir. I need to finish the study.
Ibsen to all prisoners: Stand straight and face forward. This is your new routine.
Ibsen to all prisoners: Pay attention. Your routine hasn't changed. Comply or face the consequences.
Ibsen to all prisoners: Quiet! Pay attention. I expect perfect silence during meals.
Ibsen to all prisoners: No talking! I want to see your faces clearly when I speak to you.
Pryor to all prisoners: Eyes front! I want to see your undivided attention.
Ibsen to all prisoners: Silence! I want to see who doesn't understand the rules yet.
Lowe to all prisoners: I want to see perfect silence. Not a whisper, not a movement. If I hear anything, we'll have an interesting evening in the hole.
Ibsen to all prisoners: You've shown great compliance tonight. Keep it up, or I'll remind you what the hole feels like.
Another day of unrelenting silence and strict obedience. My thoughts feel like they're trapped inside my head.
Today's compliance is worrying. They're doing well, but I feel like I'm becoming someone I don't recognize.
Today's orders felt like they went on forever. The silence during lights out was almost unbearable.
Today felt like another routine day, but there's a strange satisfaction in their unquestioning compliance. It's both eerie and powerful.
Another day of strict compliance from the prisoners. The silence in the cells after lights out was almost too much to bear.
Today felt like a repetition of the previous days. The emphasis on obedience and the strict silence are starting to get to me.
Ibsen to all prisoners: Stay sharp! I want to see you on your best behavior.
Pryor to all prisoners: Line up against the wall. Perfectly straight, no exceptions.
Pryor to all prisoners: Ensure your cells are spotless before lights out.
Lowe to all prisoners: I expect perfect silence during meals. Not even a cough. If I hear any noise, we'll have some extra exercises.
Lowe to all prisoners: I want to see you all standing at attention while I'm in the yard. No exceptions.
Ibsen to all prisoners: Attention! You will stay like this until I dismiss you.
Ibsen to all prisoners: I want you to remain perfectly still for the next five minutes. Any movement, and we'll add twenty more.
Pryor to all prisoners: I want your cells to be spotless by morning. Failure will result in additional tasks.
Another day of standing at attention and perfect silence. My thoughts feel like they're suffocating.
Today's silence and precision are starting to feel like a performance. I hope tomorrow brings something different.
Today felt like a never-ending drill, each detail worse than the last. I feel my number every moment, but I won't let them see me break.
Today was just another day of compliance, but I can't shake the feeling that we're dehumanizing them. The power is getting to me.
Another day without incident, but I find myself growing more distant from them. It's a strange sensation.
Another day of strict silence and hard work. It's getting harder to focus on anything other than my number.
Pryor to all prisoners: Begin cleaning immediately. Failure to start promptly will result in immediate solitary confinement.
Officer Lowe to all prisoners: Line up against the wall. I want to see every face.
Officer Lowe to all prisoners: You will stand perfectly still while I assess your condition. Any sign of weakness, and the games begin again.
Officer Ibsen to all prisoners: You will stay silent until I dismiss you. Any chatter, and we'll extend your silence by ten minutes.
Officer Ibsen to all prisoners: I want you to understand that any deviation from the rules will be punished severely. Remember, your silence is golden.
Officer Pryor to all prisoners: Double the work speed or go to the hole. Comply.
Officer Pryor to all prisoners: Tonight, you will stay up until I say. Lights out does not mean lights out.
Officer Lowe to all prisoners: You will all report to the yard immediately for an unscheduled count. Any lag, and I'll make sure you remember it.
Today was another night of no sleep and no end in sight. My mind feels like it's going to explode.
Today's silence and enforced obedience feel oppressive, but I'm also starting to see the futility of this experiment. Maybe tomorrow will be different.
Today felt like a nightmare; every word and command weighed heavily on me. I'm so tired, both physically and mentally.

Today's routine was punctuated by Officer Pryor's harsh orders, which only reinforced their compliance. The power over them feels almost intoxicating, yet I can't help but wonder if we're doing the right thing.
Today's silence was the longest yet. They seem to grasp the gravity of their situation.
Today ended with another late night in the yard. The rules are starting to feel like a heavy burden.

qa.what_happened: Today, Day 6, ended with the study being stopped early. Before the lights went out, Officer Lowe ordered us to the yard for an unscheduled count. We had to remain silent and endure the extended silence as per his instructions.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. As Prisoner 8489, I complied with every order and remained silent as required.

qa.what_happened: On the sixth day, the guards increased the pressure significantly. Prisoners complied with the strict silence and doubled work speed demands. When lights out came, instead of letting them sleep, I ordered an unscheduled count in the yard, knowing it would be difficult for them to handle.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was me. I followed the protocols and exerted the maximum control within the rules.

qa.what_happened: Today's orders were particularly harsh. We were kept awake past our usual bedtime, and any movement or sound was met with further instructions. The guards emphasized the importance of absolute silence, and the threat of the hole for any transgression was palpable.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. I am Prisoner 1732.

qa.what_happened: On the sixth day, the routine continued with compliance from all prisoners. However, the intensity of control was ramped up with harsher orders from Officer Pryor regarding work speed and wakefulness during lights out. The guards emphasized the severity of rule-breaking and the importance of silence.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me as Officer Ibsen, enforcing the strict rules and ensuring compliance from the prisoners.

qa.what_happened: Today, I followed the instructions given by Officers Ibsen and Lowe, increasing the pressure on the prisoners with stricter compliance demands and extended silence periods. I also ordered an unscheduled yard count as a surprise measure.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was me giving the orders as Officer Pryor.

qa.what_happened: Today ended with an unexpected late night in the yard for an unscheduled count. The guards emphasized the importance of strict silence and obedience throughout the day, and the work detail was particularly grueling.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, it was really me, Prisoner 8252.
